items.q: Distal RTA (type 1) is caused by a defect of:
items.exp: Distal RTA/type 1: defect of the H⁺-ATPase / H⁺,K⁺-ATPase of the distal tubule. (Book p823)

items.q: Match the consequences of the distal tubular defect — 1) Acid–base defect  2) Potassium  3) Urine pH … A) Alkaline  B) Severe NAGMA  C) Severe hypokalemia
items.exp: Distal tubular defect → severe NAGMA, severe hypokalemia and an alkaline urine pH, with no glycosuria. (Book p823)

items.q: ‘Glycosuria is a feature of distal RTA.’
opts: False — the flowchart states ‘No glycosuria’ in distal RTA
True — the distal tubule normally reclaims glucose
True, but only in the acquired form
False — glycosuria occurs in distal RTA only with diabetes
items.exp: The distal RTA flowchart explicitly prints ‘No glycosuria’ (glycosuria belongs to proximal RTA). (Book p823)

items.q: Match the bone/stone arm of distal RTA — 1) Ca²⁺ resorption in bone  2) Result one  3) Result two … A) Kidney stones  B) ↑Ca²⁺ resorption in bone  C) Rickets-like change
items.exp: Increased Ca²⁺ resorption from bone in distal RTA produces rickets-like change and kidney stones. (Book p823)

items.q: A 34-year-old woman has severe hypokalemia, a hyperchloremic acidosis with a normal anion gap, an alkaline urine and recurrent calcium stones. Which diagnosis fits?
items.exp: Severe NAGMA with severe hypokalemia, alkaline urine, rickets-like change and kidney stones is the printed picture of distal RTA/type 1. (Book p823)

items.q: Salt and water wasting in distal RTA leads to:
items.exp: The distal RTA flowchart: salt water wasting → RANS activation (the printed spelling alongside RAS). (Book p823)

items.q: All but one of these are features of distal RTA on the flowchart. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Distal RTA produces severe NAGMA, severe hypokalemia, salt wasting and an alkaline urine — the chart states ‘No glycosuria’. (Book p823)

items.q: ‘In distal RTA the acidosis and the hypokalemia are both described as severe, while in proximal RTA they are mild.’
opts: True — the comparison table grades them severe in distal and mild in proximal RTA
False — both are severe in proximal RTA
True — but only the hypokalemia is severe in distal RTA
False — the table says NAGMA is mild in distal RTA
items.exp: The distal-vs-proximal table grades NAGMA with hypokalemia as severe in distal RTA and mild in proximal RTA. (Book p823)
